evidence: Here, we perform high-throughput density functional theory calculations to screen 236 layered semiconductors and identify candidates with low effective mass (m*) and weak POP scattering.
Notably, GaGe2Te stands out with exceptionally high cross-plane sigma and power factor, enabled by a favorable combination of small m* and a small ionic dielectric constant.
Simultaneously, GaGe2Te exhibits an ultralow cross-plane kappa(L) of 0.57 W m(-1) K-1 at 300 K, originating from weak interlayer bonding and pronounced phonon anharmonicity.
The structure of the new compound GaGe2Te has been determined using nanofocused synchrotron radiation.
The trigonal structure (space group P 3? ${\overline{3}}$ m1, a=4.0443(3) & ANGS;, c=14.923(2) & ANGS;, V=211.38(4) & ANGS;(3); Z=2) consists of Ge bilayers sandwiched by Ga-Te layers.
Ge and Ga are tetrahedrally coordinated.
The structure resembles that of GaGeTe but features an additional Ge atom layer.
DFT calculations suggest only a small extent of charge transfer, which is confirmed by both Bader and Mulliken charges.
